s: The Night Watcher Helps you see in the dark, keeps your skin and eyes healthy, and helps your body fight germs. Carrots Sweet potato Spinach Mango Pumpkin Eggs Retinol & retinyl esters Beta-carotene Alpha-carotene & beta-cryptoxanthin Retinal & retinoic acid Lutein, zeaxanthin & lycopene
Vitamin A that's ready to use the moment you eat it. It comes from animal foods.
Colorful plant pigments that your body turns into vitamin A only when it needs it.

The Spark Plug Turns the food you eat into fuel your body can actually use, especially carbs. Whole grains Beans & lentils Sunflower seeds Peanuts Fortified bread & cereal Fish Thiamine Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) Benfotiamine

The Glow-Getter Helps every cell make energy and keeps your skin, eyes and mouth in good shape. Milk Yogurt Eggs Almonds Mushrooms Spinach Riboflavin FMN (flavin mononucleotide) FAD (flavin adenine dinucleotide)

The Fire Starter Helps turn food into energy and keeps your skin, tummy and brain running smoothly. Peanuts Mushrooms Brown rice Chicken Tuna Fortified cereal Nicotinic acid Nicotinamide (niacinamide) NAD & NADP Tryptophan

Mr. Everywhere Helps your body break down fats, carbs and protein, and helps make some hormones. Avocado Mushrooms Sunflower seeds Broccoli Sweet potato Eggs Pantothenic acid Calcium pantothenate Pantethine Coenzyme A Panthenol

The Mood Chef Helps your body use protein and cooks up brain chemicals that affect mood and sleep. Chickpeas (hi, hummus!) Bananas Potatoes Salmon Chicken Fortified cereal Pyridoxine Pyridoxal Pyridoxamine PLP & PMP
The Hair Hype Helps turn food into energy, and is famous (maybe too famous) for hair, skin and nails. Cooked eggs Almonds Sweet potato Sunflower seeds Spinach Salmon Biotin (D-biotin) Biocytin

The Builder Helps make and repair DNA and build brand-new cells, including red blood cells. Leafy greens Lentils & beans Broccoli Avocado Oranges Fortified bread & cereal Food folate Folic acid L-methylfolate (5-MTHF)

The Nerve Guardian Keeps your nerves healthy and helps make red blood cells and DNA. Eggs Milk & cheese Fish Meat Fortified plant milks Fortified cereal Cyanocobalamin Hydroxocobalamin Methylcobalamin Adenosylcobalamin

The Citrus Superhero Builds collagen (your body's glue), helps heal cuts and keeps your immune system ready for action. Oranges Bell peppers Kiwi Strawberries Broccoli Tomatoes Ascorbic acid Sodium & calcium ascorbate Dehydroascorbic acid

The Sunshine Buddy Helps your body grab calcium from food to build strong bones and teeth. Sunshine (on your skin) Fortified milk Salmon Egg yolks Mushrooms grown in UV light Fortified cereal & juice Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) Vitamin D2 (ergocalciferol) Calcidiol (25-hydroxyvitamin D) Calcitriol
The kind your skin makes from sunshine. It's also the most common kind in supplements.
The plant-and-fungus kind of vitamin D, made by mushrooms and yeast in UV light.

The Bodyguard Protects your cells from damage, like a bodyguard for every cell in your body. Sunflower seeds Almonds Peanut butter Spinach Avocado Plant oils Alpha-tocopherol Beta, gamma & delta-tocopherol Tocotrienols (alpha, beta, gamma, delta) Natural vs. lab-made labels
Four forms of vitamin E, and alpha-tocopherol is the one your body keeps.
Four lesser-known forms of vitamin E, found mainly in certain oils and grains.

The Patch-Up Pro Helps your blood clot so cuts stop bleeding, and helps keep your bones strong. Kale & spinach Broccoli Lettuce Soybeans Collard & turnip greens Soybean & canola oil Vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) Vitamin K2 (menaquinones) MK-4 MK-7 Vitamin K3 (menadione)
The main kind of vitamin K in food, made by green plants.
A family of vitamin K forms made by bacteria. Find them in fermented foods and some animal foods.
